source.method: straight-line fit to the published characteristic curve over one log H window shared by all three channels, [-2.36, -0.46], on Fujifilm's printed lux-second axis, anchored at the sheet's printed ISO 400/27° through the ISO 5800 speed point (green and the slower of red and blue, each at minimum density plus 0.15), which sits 0.16 log H (about 0.5 stop) faster on that axis than ISO 400 predicts, a shift of +0.16, which makes the window Kodak's [-2.2, -0.3]

name: Fujifilm Superia Premium 400
note: Dye gammas are this stock's own, read off its maker's published characteristic curve. Nothing here is measured from a roll. Read from Fujifilm Japan's own sheet for the Japan-market film sold as Fujicolor Superia Premium 400. Fujifilm names no other stock it shares an emulsion with, so it stands on its own. Fujifilm's sheets print lux-seconds, but their ISO 5800 speed points do not sit where Kodak's do, so the window is anchored at the printed speed like every sheet not on Kodak's footing.
